items.title: Dow surges nearly 550 points on strong earnings; chip stocks weigh on Nasdaq
items.content: Dow Jones added ~550 points on Tuesday, July 28, driven by strong earnings reports. However, chip stocks weighed on Nasdaq amid China semiconductor competition fears. S&P 500 closed little changed.

items.title: Stock market today: Dow closes higher, Hang Seng up 0.31%
items.content: Dow gained 262 points (+0.51%) to 52,210 on Monday. Tuesday's session saw Dow adding ~550 points. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was up 0.31% in late trade, while CSI 300 closed 2.83% lower at 4,569.52.

items.title: Iran War Updates: US thwarts Iranian missile attack; Strait crossings collapse
items.content: Only 29 verified Strait of Hormuz crossings recorded from July 24-26, down sharply after ceasefire collapsed. Iran targeted several vessels. US and Iran returned to mediated talks in Oman with military action temporarily suspended.

items.title: China's AI chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
items.content: China's progress in developing deep ultraviolet lithography machines sparked concerns among investors for major semiconductor stocks. Morningstar analyst warned market was 'spooked' by threat to competitive position of global chip leaders.

items.title: Tech Stocks Tumble on Worries Over AI Spending and China's Chips
items.content: Sell-off driven by fears about ballooning AI infrastructure spending by big tech and threat of cheaper competitors. Cheaper AI models threaten dominance of US-listed companies, while China competition loosened South Korea's grip on memory chip market.

items.title: China's CXMT Stock Soars 470% on Debut in AI Race
items.content: CXMT, China's leading memory chipmaker, soared 470% on its first trading day, becoming the most valuable company on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

items.title: China stocks slide to one-week low as AI valuation concerns hit tech
items.content: Chinese stocks fell to a one-week low led by sharp selloff in technology and semiconductor shares as investors questioned AI-driven valuations amid CXMT IPO frenzy.

items.title: Forecasts for June PCE Show Cooling Inflation Ahead of Fed's Meeting
items.content: Economists expect core PCE to edge down to 3.3% annual rate in June, from 3.4% in May. Overall PCE expected at 3.8%. Month-over-month reading shows PCE could rise just 0.04% in June.

items.title: All eyes on Meta, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft earnings this week
items.content: Big week for tech earnings: Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft all set to report quarterly results, with AI spending and chip competition as key themes.

items.title: WTI Crude Steady Near $81 on Fed and Geopolitical Risks
items.content: WTI crude steady near $81 after touching one-week low. Markets reduce geopolitical risk premium as US-Iran tensions ease and diplomatic talks continue in Oman.

items.title: Weekly commentary: Markets react less sharply to Middle East escalation
items.content: BlackRock notes markets have reacted less sharply to latest Middle East escalation even as global economy has fewer buffers against prolonged energy shock. Investors pricing in temporary disruption rather than protracted conflict.

items.title: Fed, BoE, BoJ meet as chips and Mag 7 report this week
items.content: Hang Seng Index rose 1.6% last week, fourth straight weekly gain, closing just below 25,000. Key week ahead with central bank decisions from Fed, BoE, BoJ and major tech earnings.

items.title: Iran's economy hit as scope of US war grows beyond Hormuz
items.content: US and Iran returned to mediated talks with military action temporarily suspended. War continues to impact international maritime corridors beyond Strait of Hormuz and domestic markets.
